subject: Approval request: FinCloud phased scaleback & early-exit amendment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-05-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Approval request: FinCloud phased scaleback & early-exit amendment

Team —

Quick summary: FinCloud (prospect->closed in Apr) is asking for two non-standard contract items before countersigning the SOW:

1) A one-time early-exit option after month 9 with a 60-day notice window; they prefer no monetary penalty but are open to a prorated credit model.
2) A phased scaleback (they call it a "phased scaledown") to reduce committed capacity by up to 50% over three quarters if usage drops, with an agreed ramp schedule and usage verification.

Attachments: FinCloud_SOW_v3.pdf (current SOW) and phased_scaleback_matrix.xlsx (customer-proposed ramp schedule).

Why we're escalating: these touches change our standard committed spend guarantees and could materially affect first-year ARR. Sales is recommending we accept a limited version of this to close the deal quickly. I need legal and finance sign-off on the exact language and any required termination fee or clawback. If we approve, sales will produce an amendment and push DocuSign.

My suggested compromise to present to the customer (sales-proposed):
- Allow a single opt-out after month 9 with 60 days' notice.
- If they opt out, provide either (A) prorated refund of prepaid committed credits OR (B) a termination fee equal to 25% of remaining committed value (whichever we choose).
- Phased scaleback: allow reductions of 20% per quarter up to 50% total across three quarters; reductions are effective only after 60 days' notice and verified usage doesn't exceed new baseline for 30 days.
- Cap discounts/price concessions to 20% for year 1; clawback if committed minimums not met.

Requested ask: legal + finance, please confirm whether this structure is acceptable or propose alternative guardrails (single opt-out only, fee amount, required logs, any prohibitions). Sales wants to reply to FinCloud by end of week.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

[Attachment: FinCloud_SOW_v3.pdf] [Attachment: phased_scaleback_matrix.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-25T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request: FinCloud phased scaleback & early-exit amendment

Ben —

Thanks for flagging. From a go-to-market standpoint I'm in favor of a conditional approval to preserve the deal while limiting downside. A couple of practical asks I want in the amendment:
- Define measurable success metrics (p95 latency, tokens/second, error rate) tied to the opt-out — otherwise they can claim "poor performance" without evidence.
- Limit opt-out to one exercise over the term (single use).
- Add a short "post-mortem/cure" clause: if customer submits evidence of perf gap, we get 30 days to remediate before the opt-out becomes effective.
- Make the prorated refund option subject to reconciliation against reserved vs. actual usage to avoid double credits.

If legal is comfortable with the single-use opt-out + cure period, I'm happy to accept 25% termination fee OR prorated credit (we should pick one; I lean to fee for predictability). Also happy to accept the phased scaleback as proposed if finance gets comfortable with the revenue profile.

I'll stand by to help draft the customer-facing language.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Sales
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: none]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-26T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request: FinCloud phased scaleback & early-exit amendment

Thanks — I've reviewed the customer request and Ben/Marissa's proposed compromise. High level legal position: acceptable with a few mandatory redlines. Key points:

1) Single-use opt-out: yes — limit to a single exercise per 12-month period (or single occurrence in the term) and require 60 days' written notice.
2) Evidence & verification: require the customer to provide a specific evidence package (usage logs, timestamps, and APM traces) and a defined SLA metric (we should insert thresholds). Include an independent verification step (our ops team confirms logs).
3) Cure period: require 30 calendar days from our delivery of remediation plan; opt-out only effective if unresolved after cure window.
4) Financial mechanics: do not allow unconditional prorated refunds. We should offer two structured outcomes: (A) a termination fee set at 25% of unused committed value OR (B) a prorated credit against future Redwood services but not cash refunds. Whichever option we present must be mutual choice at negotiation; prefer the fee for cash predictability.
5) Downsell protections: specify minimum committed spend for first 6 months to avoid immediate churn gaming.
6) Data/security: no changes to data residency, retention or audit rights.

I've attached a redline (SOW_redline_karthik.docx) with clause language for the amendment.

If finance agrees to the fee % and minimums, legal is ok to sign off on the language and proceed to DocuSign.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
[Attachment: SOW_redline_karthik.docx]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-27T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request: FinCloud phased scaleback & early-exit amendment

Ben/Team —

I've modeled the proposal quickly (see attached financial_impact_runway.xlsx). Summary:
- If we allow a single opt-out with a 25% termination fee: net first-year ARR drops ~14% vs base case but cash is mostly preserved.
- If we accept prorated cash refunds: worst-case ARR and cash hit is materially higher (up to 35% drop in year 1), which is not acceptable.

My recommendation: accept the single-use opt-out but with the following finance guardrails:
- Require a minimum committed spend of $1.2M over the first 12 months (this is the minimum I will accept for this deal to proceed).
- Termination fee: 25% of remaining committed value if they opt out.
- Phased scaleback: allowed per proposed schedule (20%/quarter) but only after the initial 6-month period. No retroactive refunds; reductions apply only to future invoices after verification.
- Cap year-1 discount at 20% and include a usage-based clawback for the first 12 months.

If legal is comfortable with the verification language and Marissa is comfortable moving with a 25% fee and $1.2M committed minimum, I approve proceeding to amendment and DocuSign.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Director, Sales Operations & Revenue Strategy
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
[Attachment: financial_impact_runway.xlsx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Approval request: FinCloud phased scaleback & early-exit amendment

Ben / team —

Executive sign-off granted with the conditions below. Thank you for consolidating the risk analysis. Conditions to include in the amendment and SOW addendum before DocuSign:

1) Single opt-out allowed once after month 9 with 60 days' written notice. Opt-out subject to: (a) submission of the evidence package specified by Legal, (b) our 30-day cure period, and (c) verification by Redwood ops.
2) Termination mechanics: customer may choose either (A) a 25% termination fee on remaining committed value OR (B) a prorated credit applied to future Redwood services only (no cash refunds). Default choice will be (A) unless customer explicitly requests (B) and Finance approves in writing.
3) Minimum committed spend: $1,200,000 over the first 12 months. If they do not commit to this minimum, deal cannot proceed with the requested opt-out/scaleback language.
4) Phased scaleback: permitted reductions of 20% per quarter (max 50% across three quarters) and only effective after verification and a 60-day notice. Reductions apply to future invoices; no retroactive credits.
5) Discount cap: 20% in year 1 with a usage clawback tied to actual tokens consumed or invoices.
6) All redline language from Legal to be included; amendment must be countersigned by our CFO before execution.

Once Ben confirms we have customer agreement on the minimum commit and fee structure, Sales may proceed to prepare the amendment and send the DocuSign link. Update HubSpot deal FC-2025-019 with the amendment and attach the financial model for the audit trail.

Approved — proceed accordingly.

Laura Bennett
VP, Finance & Revenue Operations
laura.bennett@redwood.com
[Attachment: none]
